problem: Find the angle between $a=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 0 \\ 6\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

feedback.problem: Find the angle between $a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
feedback.worked_solution:
Rearranging the dot product formula, we have: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,a\,||\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}+{a}_{z}^{2}}\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot (-1)+3\cdot 2}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{3}^{2}}\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{11}{\sqrt{14}\cdot \sqrt{9}} \\  & =\frac{11}{3\sqrt{14}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{11}{3\sqrt{14}})≈{11.49}^{∘}.
$$
